analysis: The PR is documentation-only. docs/architecture/security/encryption.md gains a 'Provider cache storage' section (head lines 176-228). It covers: DBK3-encrypted cache payloads with keys in the SE/Keychain hierarchy; `darkbloom cache set --directory` accepting an APFS private directory, with external volumes requiring APFS encryption and a pinned filesystem UUID; `CacheVolume.inspect` and `CacheStorage.validateOpenedDirectory` checks. It states these are not peripheral attestation and that relocation leaves old ciphertext behind. docs/consumer/verification.md (lines 253-255) and docs/provider/attestation.md (patch near line 321) add a note that cache-volume checks are not part of the coordinator's attestation verdict. This is consistent with TB-009/TB-011, and no change to coordinator trust, App Attest or legacy authorization semantics is claimed. Coordinator, registry and provider-swift code (CacheVolume.swift, CacheStorage.swift, SSDNoFollowIO.swift) was not supplied, so the doc claims are unverified: no redirect to another disk, UUID validation at open time, and keys not copied to the payload volume. The one finding is the threat-model gap for relocatable or external cache storage (T-041, T-016). The next pass should check the cache code against the doc, and check whether the canonical T-041 text mentions cache location. TB-002/TB-009 interactions are unchanged.

findings.detail: The new 'Provider cache storage' section describes a `darkbloom cache set --directory` feature that moves encrypted KV-cache payloads to external APFS volumes. Its trust checks are a pinned filesystem UUID, ownership and flag checks, and an APFS-encryption requirement. The doc itself says these are not peripheral attestation. A malicious or cloned controller can defeat the UUID pin, retain ciphertext, delete or replay still-valid ciphertext, and supply traffic-analysis metadata (sizes, times, model/layout binding). Switching locations also leaves stale ciphertext in the old location with no secure erase. The canonical model covers the SSD cache under T-041 and disk-fill DoS under T-016. It has no threat or mitigation for removable or untrusted storage, UUID-clone spoofing, replay of valid ciphertext, or orphaned ciphertext after relocation. Trigger: an operator, or an adversarial provider, points the cache at an attacker-influenced volume. Impact: availability and metadata leakage, and possible replay of cache blocks within the TTL. Fix: add a TB-003/T-041 threat entry covering relocatable cache storage, with the documented mitigations and residuals (authenticated encryption, TTL and tenant binding, no peripheral attestation, no secure erase on relocation). Confirm the code matches the doc's claims. The code was not supplied in this batch.
findings.title: Threat model lacks coverage for relocatable external-volume provider cache storage
